articles.title: Two large asteroids found spinning as fast as a fairground ride
articles.summary: Rocks in the asteroid belt rotating at ultra-fast speeds suggest our understanding of asteroid structure might be wrong
articles.content:
Rocks in the asteroid belt rotating at ultra-fast speeds suggest our understanding of asteroid structure might be wrong

Some asteroids spin surprisingly fast ronib1979/iStockphoto/Getty Images

Large asteroids have been found spinning so fast they should break apart, suggesting they might be stronger than we thought.

Dmitrii Vavilov at the University of Washington in Seattle and his colleagues analysed some of the first data collected by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, which began a 10-year survey of the sky in June 2026. From a sample of more than 9000 asteroids, they measured the rotation of 260, based on a change in their brightness caused by the spinning asteroids’ irregular shapes.

Of these, 66 were deemed to be super-fast rotators, spinning quickly enough to complete a rotation in less than 2.2 hours, a limit at which asteroids should no longer be able to hold themselves together under their own gravity.

Advertisement

Two space rocks in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter were even more unusual ultra-fast rotators. Each was larger than 2 kilometres wide, but completed a full spin once every 5 minutes, something never seen before for such big asteroids.

“On the scale of billions of years, asteroids of this size should hit each other and reaccumulate,” says Vavilov, forming loose conglomerations of material known as rubble piles that would break apart when rotating rapidly. The high rotation speed suggests that these asteroids aren’t rubble piles, but instead monolithic objects at least 30 times stronger than clay, says Vavilov.

This probably means our models of how asteroids have smashed together over the 4.6-billion-year history of the solar system aren’t correct, he says. That might mean these are pristine objects from the early solar system.

The universe: Reality or simulation? See Catherine Heymans at New Scientist Live 2026 Find out more

Other fast-spinning asteroids have been spotted before, but nothing as large as these two. Standing on their surface, a person would travel at more than 100 kilometres per hour (over 60 miles per hour), much slower than Earth’s equatorial rotation of 1670 km/h (1040 mph). But because of the smaller size of the asteroids, it would feel “like a rollercoaster”, says Vavilov, and clinging to the surface would be difficult.

The asteroids might have been spun up by the sun heating their surfaces and giving them torque, known as the YORP effect, but that in itself is uncertain because of their large distance from the sun. “That’s another mystery,” says Vavilov, who hopes to study the asteroids in more detail in future.
articles.reasoning: The discovery of large asteroids spinning at ultra-fast speeds challenges existing scientific models of asteroid structure and solar system history, representing a significant breakthrough in space science with broad implications for our understanding of planetary formation and asteroid composition.
articles.personality_title: Two large asteroids found spinning faster than expected, challenging asteroid science
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Asteroids are rocky objects that orbit the Sun, mostly found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Scientists usually think big asteroids spin slowly because if they spin too fast, they should break apart.

**What happened** – Researchers from the University of Washington studied data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, which started a 10-year sky survey in 2026. They looked at over 9,000 asteroids and found 66 that spin faster than the usual limit of 2.2 hours per rotation. Two of these asteroids, each more than 2 kilometers wide, spin once every 5 minutes – a speed never seen before for such large rocks.

**Impact** – This discovery suggests these asteroids are much stronger than scientists thought. Instead of being loose piles of rubble, they might be solid rock, at least 30 times stronger than clay. This challenges the current ideas about how asteroids form and survive impacts over billions of years. It also means these asteroids could be original pieces from the early solar system.

**What's next step** – Scientists want to study these asteroids more closely to understand why they spin so fast and how they became so strong. They are also curious about how the sun might affect their spin, a process called the YORP effect, though this is still uncertain.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Two large asteroids spinning at record speeds reveal they are stronger and more mysterious than previously believed, changing how we understand asteroid history and structure.
articles.personality_title_fr: Deux gros astéroïdes tournent plus vite que prévu, remettant en question la science des astéroïdes
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les astéroïdes sont des roches qui tournent autour du Soleil, principalement dans la ceinture d’astéroïdes entre Mars et Jupiter. Les scientifiques pensent généralement que les gros astéroïdes tournent lentement, car s’ils tournent trop vite, ils devraient se briser.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Des chercheurs de l’Université de Washington ont étudié des données de l’observatoire Vera C. Rubin au Chili, qui a commencé une étude du ciel sur 10 ans en 2026. Ils ont examiné plus de 9 000 astéroïdes et trouvé 66 qui tournent plus vite que la limite normale de 2,2 heures par rotation. Deux de ces astéroïdes, chacun plus large que 2 kilomètres, tournent en seulement 5 minutes – une vitesse jamais vue pour des roches aussi grandes.

**Impact** – Cette découverte suggère que ces astéroïdes sont beaucoup plus solides que ce que les scientifiques pensaient. Au lieu d’être des tas de débris, ils pourraient être des roches solides, au moins 30 fois plus fortes que l’argile. Cela remet en cause les idées actuelles sur la formation des astéroïdes et leur survie aux collisions pendant des milliards d’années. Cela signifie aussi que ces astéroïdes pourraient être des morceaux originaux du système solaire primitif.

**Prochaine étape** – Les scientifiques veulent étudier ces astéroïdes de plus près pour comprendre pourquoi ils tournent aussi vite et comment ils sont devenus si solides. Ils s’interrogent aussi sur l’effet du soleil sur leur rotation, appelé effet YORP, bien que cela reste incertain.

**En une phrase** – Deux gros astéroïdes tournant à une vitesse record montrent qu’ils sont plus solides et mystérieux que prévu, changeant notre compréhension de leur histoire et structure.
articles.personality_title_es: Dos grandes asteroides giran más rápido de lo esperado, desafiando la ciencia de los asteroides
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los asteroides son rocas que orbitan alrededor del Sol, principalmente en el cinturón de asteroides entre Marte y Júpiter. Los científicos suelen pensar que los asteroides grandes giran despacio porque si giraran muy rápido, deberían romperse.

¿Qué pasó** – Investigadores de la Universidad de Washington estudiaron datos del Observatorio Vera C. Rubin en Chile, que comenzó un estudio del cielo de 10 años en 2026. Examinaron más de 9,000 asteroides y encontraron 66 que giran más rápido que el límite normal de 2.2 horas por rotación. Dos de estos asteroides, cada uno más grande que 2 kilómetros, completan una vuelta cada 5 minutos, una velocidad nunca vista en rocas tan grandes.

**Impacto** – Este hallazgo sugiere que estos asteroides son mucho más fuertes de lo que los científicos pensaban. En lugar de ser pilas de escombros, podrían ser rocas sólidas, al menos 30 veces más fuertes que la arcilla. Esto desafía las ideas actuales sobre cómo se forman los asteroides y cómo sobreviven a los golpes durante miles de millones de años. También significa que estos asteroides podrían ser piezas originales del sistema solar temprano.

**Próximo paso** – Los científicos quieren estudiar estos asteroides más de cerca para entender por qué giran tan rápido y cómo se volvieron tan fuertes. También están interesados en cómo el sol puede afectar su giro, un proceso llamado efecto YORP, aunque todavía es incierto.

**Conclusión en una frase** – Dos grandes asteroides girando a velocidades récord muestran que son más fuertes y misteriosos de lo que se pensaba, cambiando cómo entendemos su historia y estructura.
